next_item_hypothesis: For the observed directed transitions, especially the repeated source-to-destination edges 22372→9218 and 22372→22639 (with the latter pair also observed in reverse), a flat metric may allocate content-near but transition-distinct items to the same early residual-code neighborhoods. A negatively curved squared distance may better separate branching, non-reciprocal transition neighborhoods while retaining a globally balanced assignment. This is a falsifiable hypothesis about item-SID construction, not a claim that the measured directionality proves negative curvature or improves recommendation.

geometry_constants.stable_arcosh: For z>=1 compute arcosh(z)=log1p((z-1)+sqrt((z-1)*(z+1))); clamp z to max(z,1.0) only. Do not impose a floor above 1.0.
geometry_constants.domain_policy: For c>0, project every scored vector into the closed Euclidean ball of radius R=(1-epsilon)/sqrt(c); scored input coordinates must satisfy c*||x||^2<1 and c*||y||^2<1. Non-finite values fail closed. At c=0 use the same fixed ball ||x||<=R=0.999, the identity projection when already in the ball and radial projection otherwise; do not evaluate (1-epsilon)/sqrt(c), which is undefined.

operator.scored_distance_squared: D_c^2(x,y)=(1/c)*arcosh(1+2*c*||x-y||^2/((1-c*||x||^2)*(1-c*||y||^2)))^2, with the arcosh argument clamped only below at 1.0 and arcosh evaluated by the log1p form in geometry_constants.
operator.exponential_map: Not used. The scored coordinates are the projected latent and projected code vectors directly. At c=0 the exponential map, if considered, has identity limit and is absent from the common scoring path.
operator.projection_limit: The curvature-derived radius (1-epsilon)/sqrt(c) is undefined at c=0; the flat arm instead uses the same fixed R=0.999 and the same radial projection operator as the curved arm.

assignment_algorithm.population: All N=24556 distinct items in the frozen training item inventory, in ascending stable item-ID order; no validation/test items, events, or batch-derived population. At each residual level, recompute costs on this same complete population once per epoch.
assignment_algorithm.conditioning: Level 1 conditions on no earlier code. Level 2 conditions on the frozen hard level-1 code only. Level 3 conditions on the frozen hard level-1 and level-2 codes only. There is one global codebook of 256 vectors at each level; each complete item receives one global three-code SID.
assignment_algorithm.cost_and_transport: At level l, let r_i^l be the projected residual before assignment and let e_{l,k} be the trainable raw code vector. Let v_{l,k}=Project(e_{l,k}) using the shared fixed projection. Define C^l_{ik}=D_c^2(r_i^l,v_{l,k}) using the scored squared distance. Set u^l_{ik}=-C^l_{ik}/tau and a_i=max_k u^l_{ik}; define A^l_{ik}=exp(u^l_{ik}-a_i), which is finite and uniquely row-normalized up to the stated deterministic arithmetic. Initialize Q^l=A^l. Perform exactly 100 full-population alternating normalizations in fixed order: Q_ik <- Q_ik*(1/N)/sum_j Q_ij for every row i, then Q_ik <- Q_ik*(1/256)/sum_j Q_jk for every column k. Use float64, stable item-ID/code-ID reduction order, and no minibatch statistics. If any denominator is zero or non-finite, fail closed. The resulting transport Q is uniquely determined by the frozen input, code vectors, constants, initialization and iteration order; it is a fixed-iteration globally balanced soft assignment, not an optimal-transport solve. Its row and column targets are explicitly 1/N and 1/256; no smoothing is applied to Q.
assignment_algorithm.discrete_label_extraction: For each level independently, sort all N item rows by the tuple (-Q^l_{i,0},..., -Q^l_{i,255}, stable_item_ID), lexicographically ascending, and assign sorted rank j to code j mod 256. This exact global rank rule produces deterministic hard labels with per-level code counts differing by at most one; the item ID resolves all ties. It is not a greedy repair or approximate transport solve. To prevent level-two prefix collapse, level-2 sorting is performed separately within each level-1 label group and assigned codes by rank modulo 256 within that group; if a group has fewer than 256 items, its labels remain unique up to its size. Concatenate (k1,k2,k3) in level order. Q is the soft target and this rank rule is the sole hard-label rule; no argmin rule is also used.
assignment_algorithm.arm_and_refresh: The common implementation has curvature parameter c. For each epoch, calculate all three level transports and hard labels from the complete training inventory using the current item encoder/codebooks, then hold labels fixed for that epoch's minibatch updates. Refresh once at the next epoch. Both arms use identical architecture, parameter count, initialization, optimizer, frozen 3000-epoch budget, batch size, schedule and seed identities; no sweep. Flat control sets c=0 in this same implementation and changes only D_c^2 to its exact 4*||x-y||^2 limit. No recommender/ranker, beam search, retrieval metric, user bootstrap, or validation/test supervision is part of Stage2.
assignment_algorithm.gradient_rule: Q is differentiable through costs and all fixed-count row/column normalization operations in the differentiable training loss; hard labels are stop-gradient epoch targets and are used only for residual target construction/diagnostics. For a differentiable selected code vector in the loss, use the straight-through assignment q_ST=stop_gradient(one_hot(hard_label)-Q)+Q, which has exactly the Q gradient and hard one-hot forward value. The detached epoch labels themselves carry no gradient. There is no gradient claim through sorting or hard labels.

math_definition.projection_order: At every level and for every item: (1) map the content embedding through the frozen 32-dimensional encoder to raw latent z_i; (2) radial-project z_i to r_i^1 before any distance. At each level l in order: (3) project each raw code vector e_{l,k} to v_{l,k}; (4) compute cost from the already projected residual r_i^l to projected code v_{l,k}; (5) compute full-population Q and deterministic hard label k_i^l; (6) subtract the raw code vector e_{l,k_i^l} from the current unprojected residual state s_i^l; (7) project the result to obtain the next scored residual r_i^{l+1}. Specifically s_i^1=z_i, r_i^1=Project(s_i^1); s_i^2=Project(r_i^1-e_{1,k_i^1}); s_i^3=Project(r_i^1-e_{1,k_i^1}-e_{2,k_i^2}) is NOT used: instead define s_i^2=r_i^1-e_{1,k_i^1}, r_i^2=Project(s_i^2), s_i^3=r_i^2-e_{2,k_i^2}, r_i^3=Project(s_i^3). The final SID is (k_i^1,k_i^2,k_i^3). For decoder reconstruction, sum the three raw selected code vectors, then project the sum before scored comparison. No exponential map is applied.

tensor_gradient_rules.encoder_parameters: differentiable through reconstruction, commitment, differentiable Q, and anti-collapse variance loss
tensor_gradient_rules.projected_latent_and_residuals: differentiable through radial projection (piecewise differentiable; boundary uses the analytic radial-projection derivative)
tensor_gradient_rules.raw_codebook_vectors: differentiable through projected costs, Q, straight-through reconstruction/commitment and decoder reconstruction
tensor_gradient_rules.projected_code_vectors: differentiable image of raw code vectors
tensor_gradient_rules.transport_Q: differentiable through cost and each fixed normalization; never frozen in a loss that uses its gradient
tensor_gradient_rules.hard_labels_and_sort_indices: frozen/stop-gradient for the epoch; no gradient through rank extraction
tensor_gradient_rules.straight_through_q_ST: differentiable with backward derivative exactly dQ/dparameter

objective.anti_collapse: Use variance-floor anti-collapse on the differentiable 32-dimensional raw latent, not on frozen labels: for Z in R^(N x 32), compute per-dimension population variance v_d=(1/N)*sum_i (Z_id-mean_i Z_id)^2. L_ac=(1/32)*sum_d max(0, 0.01-v_d). It enters every training minibatch loss through the epoch-frozen full-training-item latent statistics, with gradients through Z and the encoder. At complete representation collapse, every v_d=0 and L_ac=0.01 strictly positive (before its weight); its gradient is zero at the exact symmetric point, so pair it with the reconstruction and commitment terms below, whose gradients are not replaced by the detached code labels. The objective also cannot be minimized by a shared code alone because content reconstruction is computed for every item. No anti-collapse term is evaluated solely on one-hot assignments.
loss_equations: Let B be the current training-item minibatch, |B|>0; Z_B in R^(|B|x32) are mapped latents; H^l_B are the hard labels fixed for the epoch; q_ST^l in R^(|B|x256) is the straight-through assignment; V^l in R^(256x32) contains projected code vectors. Define decoded reconstruction xhat_i=Project(sum_{l=1}^3 sum_{k=1}^{256} q_ST^l[i,k]*e_{l,k}) and x_i as the frozen content embedding projected by the same shared projector. L_rec(B)=(1/|B|)*sum_{i in B} D_c^2(xhat_i,x_i). Empty B is invalid and fails closed. Target x_i is stop-gradient, so there is no target/parameter circularity.

For each level l and minibatch item i, define selected vector a_i^l=sum_k q_ST^l[i,k]*e_{l,k} and scored projected residual r_i^l using the ordered residual chain in projection_order. Let L_com(B)=(1/(3|B|))*sum_{i in B,l=1..3} ||r_i^l-stop_gradient(Project(e_{l,H_i^l}))||_2^2. The residual input is differentiable; selected code target is stop-gradient. If B is empty, fail closed. H is frozen for the epoch, so this loss has no claimed gradient through labels; it does have a direct gradient through r and encoder.

For full training item set I, Z_I in R^(N x 32), define mu_d=(1/N)*sum_i Z_id and v_d=(1/N)*sum_i(Z_id-mu_d)^2. L_ac(I)=(1/32)*sum_{d=1}^{32} max(0,0.01-v_d). Empty I is invalid. This term is evaluated from differentiable encoder outputs with gradients accumulated across the full item set, not from assignments. At collapse v_d=0 for all d and L_ac=0.01>0. The variance statistics are not detached; no target depends circularly on this loss.

The sole optimized scalar is L=1.0*L_rec(B)+1.0*L_com(B)+1.0*L_ac(I). Each sum is a mean over the explicitly stated nonempty index set; no implicit batch-level balancing or validation-derived target occurs.
See math_definition.objective.loss_equations; this key repeats the same complete equations as required by the schema, with no additional objective or target distribution.

hyperbolic_necessity: The selected measured failure is early-prefix conflation of directed, branching next-item destinations, illustrated by the frequent 22372→9218 and 22372→22639 transitions and the asymmetric edge counts across the reported graph. Negative curvature is motivated as a geometry hypothesis because it can represent expanding, hierarchical neighborhoods with less distortion than a flat metric; it is not inferred from edge directionality, and the supplied literature only verifies generative Semantic-ID next-item prediction, not a hyperbolic benefit. Stage2 diagnostics expected to respond are valid_l1_positive_hit_rate, valid_l1_hard_er, level2_distinct_prefixes, L3 collision, L3 refinement gain and conditional G3. Stage3 test_R@10 is the behavioral test. No diagnostic movement is presumed.
euclidean_control: One implementation and one architecture/parameterization are used in both arms, with the same fixed R=0.999 projection radius, projection operator, initialization, optimizer, data, seed identities, schedule and budget. The flat arm is the c->0 limit of that same code path: replace only D_c^2 by 4*||x-y||^2; the exponential map is absent in both arms. Thus the scored coordinates and feasible bounded region are identical and only the metric differs.
effect_site: Stage2 item content encoder, residual code assignment, codebook geometry and reconstruction/commitment objective; exported output is one global three-token SID per item. Stage2 does not rank or recommend.
real_trigger_measurement: Frozen current-only behavior evidence has 323633 directed pairs, 24556 distinct items, 339519 transitions, mean next-item entropy 4.844072338042215 bits and no observed reverse event for 314605 pairs (fraction 0.9266197178950221). The measured trigger is directed transition structure and branching, not evidence of curvature. The literature evidence explicitly labels the hyperbolic intersection UNKNOWN.
training_only_inputs: Frozen item content embeddings and the complete 24556-item training item inventory; only train-split item transitions may be used for optional transition regularization, and this candidate uses none. No validation/test behavior, future events, prediction-time user context, or batch-composition signals enter assignment or training targets. The frozen independent validation pairs are used only for registered diagnostics.

stage2_diagnostics.name: valid_l1_hard_er
stage2_diagnostics.seed_rule: Compute over exactly 52855 frozen validation pairs: one positive and ten negatives per anchor, seed 42, history[-1] as anchor item and target as comparison item. A positive hit is equality of anchor and positive first SID token; negative_hits counts equality for each of the ten negatives. ER=10*positive_hits/negative_hits. Promotion additionally requires the absolute frozen floor valid_l1_hard_er strictly above 10.0. Paired seed identity is [42, 43, 44]; compare curved and flat on exactly the same pair rows per seed; all seed-wise paired changes must be finite and meet the registered effect, and the arithmetic mean paired change must meet it.

stage2_diagnostics.name: level2_distinct_prefixes
stage2_diagnostics.seed_rule: Count |{(k1,k2)}| over every item in the frozen item inventory for each arm and seed. Use paired seed identities [42, 43, 44], same initialization identity and data in both arms. The absolute promotion floor is strictly above 16145. Require every seed-wise paired change and the arithmetic mean paired change to meet the registered effect.

stage2_diagnostics.name: L3_refinement_gain
stage2_diagnostics.seed_rule: For every item i, let b12(i) be the number of items with its (k1,k2), and b123(i) the number with its (k1,k2,k3). Compute mean_i log2(b12(i)/b123(i)) over the complete item inventory. Paired seed identities [42, 43, 44]; same SID inventory and seed pairing; require finite per-seed and arithmetic-mean paired changes meeting the registered effect.

stage2_diagnostics.name: conditional_G3
stage2_diagnostics.seed_rule: On each of the 52855 frozen validation pairs (anchor,target), define p_pref(l)=(n_pref(target_prefix,l)-1[l=target_k3]+1)/(b12(target)-1+256), where n_pref(q,l)=|{items j:(k1_j,k2_j)=q and k3_j=l}| and b12(q)=sum_l n_pref(q,l). Define t(a,q,l) as the train-only longest-prefix successor count from anchor item a to successor items j with prefix q and k3_j=l; T(a,q)=sum_l t(a,q,l). Define p_hist(l)=(t(a,q,l)+p_pref(l))/(T(a,q)+1). No further smoothing or renormalization is applied. G3 is the mean over all pairs of log2(p_hist(target_k3)/p_pref(target_k3)); a pair with T=0 contributes 0, and any non-finite pair makes that seed's aggregate NULL. Counts are integer item/successor counts; empty prefix buckets or zero denominators are invalid and yield NULL. Paired seed identities [42, 43, 44], require finite paired changes per seed and arithmetic mean meeting the registered effect.

stage3_behavioral_test.seed_rule: Use identical frozen Stage3 T5 protocol and paired seed identities [42, 43, 44] for curved and flat SID inputs; evaluate the test split only after Stage2 SID and diagnostics are frozen. Report paired per-seed differences and their arithmetic mean; every seed-wise difference and the mean must be finite and meet the registered effect. Test behavior is used only for this final comparison, never for Stage2 fitting, assignment, selection or tuning.

classification.falsified_if: At least one required registered stage2_diagnostics entry or stage3_behavioral_test has finite paired results for all paired seeds and its per-seed and mean changes fail its registered direction/minimum_effect, or either required absolute promotion floor in the valid_l1_hard_er / level2_distinct_prefixes seed_rule is not met.
classification.passed_if: Every registered stage2_diagnostics entry and stage3_behavioral_test has finite paired results for every paired seed, every per-seed and arithmetic-mean change meets its own registered direction/minimum_effect, and both absolute promotion floors referenced by valid_l1_hard_er and level2_distinct_prefixes are met.
classification.mixed_if: Otherwise, including any NULL seed-wise or aggregated change, zero denominator, missing evaluation, empty stratum, or comparison with any NULL seed; such an outcome is inconclusive and is neither passed nor falsified.
